PullRequest.Title: chat: preserve Chat Completions reasoning across user turns
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #338820.

A genuine follow-up user message currently drops earlier Chat Completions reasoning while retaining the assistant messages and tool calls/results. Preserve that reasoning for models that require it: recognized Kimi K3 IDs/families opt in by default, and `github.copilot.chat.modelCapabilityOverrides[modelId].thinkingInHistory` allows explicit opt-in or opt-out.

Carry the provider's actual API type and adaptive-thinking capability through the proposed language-model capability API into `ExtensionContributedChatEndpoint`. Historical Chat Completions replay requires a declared Chat Completions API; an unknown protocol fails closed. Budget-mode Messages cannot use this override to replay historical thinking. Responses and adaptive Messages retain their existing policy, and the same-model guard remains mandatory. Apply the configured family alias before choosing the outer endpoint's Kimi default.

This addresses both CCR findings. The regressions exercise the actual custom provider, outer endpoint, full `AgentPrompt` and request serializers in both history modes. This PR contains no system-notification/task-boundary changes from #338827.



CI compatibility follow-up at `d019974c81f882429025799a82c42502fa22b5be` (on the user's merged main at `c5dc4bf23e99b951b70dfca2dc48c312acaaec75`): published Insiders used by the Copilot extension-host jobs predates `LanguageModelChatApiType`. Feature-detect that enum during provider initialization and endpoint construction, leaving the protocol unknown when it is unavailable. No replay safeguard is relaxed.

Two older-host regressions reproduced both crashes before the fix and now pass. Local validation passed 82 focused tests (including the 34 reasoning-history cases), all 209 extension-host tests on published Insiders `9666ca8ea7a0ac0d0ce4e661c19f8a05d5d7ad79` (4 existing skips), the full product compile, extension type checks, changed-file ESLint and repository hygiene. The same published-host runner crashed during module initialization with the original bundle. New CI is being checked on this commit. The earlier real-model/runtime evidence below was captured at `f7c0a2a`, as recorded.

Reasoning/runtime validation head: `f7c0a2a0d4ff4235bf619ccf75278412f3532f2d`. The PR remains a draft.

- **CCR RED → GREEN:** Restore the three corrected production modules from the previous PR head `570ede977885c92722a46d0baea4cade11a2c850`: all **4** new CCR cases fail (30 other cases skipped). Restore the revised implementation: the same 4 pass. RED shows signed historical thinking incorrectly sent for budget Messages, and missing `reasoning_content` for an aliased custom deployment.
- **Final tests:** **637 passed in 16 files**, including all **34** history cases; **3** core API transport/proposal-gating tests passed. Extension TypeScript, API declaration compilation, changed-file ESLint and the normal commit hook also passed. A fresh full product build completed after removing instrumentation.
- **Real inference via the launch skill:** Local **Kimi K3 (GitHub), High**, model `kimi-k3-copilot-picker`. First turn began at `2026-09-30T10:31:32.347Z`, completed at `2026-09-30T10:31:56.070Z`; a genuine follow-up request at `2026-09-30T10:34:41.785Z` moved all three rounds into historical rendering. Actual outgoing `reasoning_text` and `reasoning_opaque` matched the original two tool-call rounds and final answer byte-for-byte (direct in-memory equality plus SHA-256/length comparisons).
- **Real controls:** `thinkingInHistory: false` excluded 4 stored Kimi rounds at `2026-09-30T10:39:53.601Z`. Switching the same chat to Gemini 3.5 Flash with replay explicitly enabled excluded all 5 older Kimi rounds at `2026-09-30T10:45:08.591Z`. Both outgoing requests contained no historical reasoning fields.
- **Scripted extension runtime:** Four public-language-model provider cases passed non-vacuous checks: budget Messages with override true omitted both historical signed blocks; adaptive Messages with override false preserved both; a Kimi family alias preserved both; unknown API with override true omitted both. Each first-turn tool continuation contained reasoning. Actual configured custom-provider metadata also crossed the real registration/selection boundary with the correct API and adaptive flags.
- **Scripted custom HTTP runtime:** The configured Chat Completions deployment with `family: 'kimi-k3'` preserved both tool-call and final-answer `reasoning_content`/`cot_id`. Repeated successfully on the clean final build without production instrumentation.

Remaining limits: standard Chat Completions deltas without an ID still reproduce independent #338819 (reasoning already absent on the first-turn continuation). Direct custom Messages HTTP trials also lacked signatures on the first-turn continuation; these are **not claimed as historical replay passes**. The budget/adaptive replay policy is verified by the signed-provider runtime fixtures and custom-provider serializer regressions. No ingestion fix is included here. Scripted providers are deterministic fixtures, not real Anthropic/custom-model inference. Combined verification with #338878 is owned by the coordinating session.

All six fields were identical on the actual follow-up request. Trace records included distinct turn/request IDs and the transition to historical rendering; this is payload evidence, not an assertion based on the model's displayed answer.

The launch skill ran against this issue's own worktree, with isolated profiles and sessions. Real-inference run: CDP 52524, extension host 52525, main 52526, agent host 52527; Playwright session `k338820-40323`. Scripted run: 55275–55278, session `k338820-76433`. Final clean build: 58617–58620, session `k338820-10418`.

Temporary instrumentation only recorded relevant model/provenance fields, reasoning lengths/hashes and exact-equality booleans. It recorded no auth headers, credentials or raw live reasoning. It has been removed from production source and the final bundle. The final clean runtime used only an external development fixture to capture its own synthetic HTTP payloads. All task-owned processes, Playwright sessions and throwaway profiles have been cleaned up.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enumerating and selecting BYOK/OpenAI-compatible language models, including OpenRouter and configured custom model groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `selectLanguageModels`/provider refresh awaits `_resolveAllLanguageModels`, the extension-host provider's `provideLanguageModelChatInformation`, existing model discovery, and the new capability projection before models become selectable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the provider model catalogue (for providers such as OpenRouter/OpenAI/Ollama)
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalogue request per provider/group resolution; returned model cardinality can be large for OpenRouter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalogue request and model metadata mapping already occurred before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The catalogue response is awaited before model selection or refresh completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and return language-model metadata between the main thread and extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC round trip per provider/group resolution, carrying one metadata record per discovered model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The RPC already carried the model catalogue; the diff adds two scalar capability fields without adding calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model selection waits for this metadata RPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered models per provider, multiplied by repeated selection/refresh calls and configured groups.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model resolutions are sequenced per vendor by `_resolveLMSequencer`; multiple vendors may resolve in parallel. The new `Promise.all` creates all endpoint projections in one burst, although the observed endpoint factories perform synchronous object construction and no additional I/O.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider model metadata may be cached internally (for example Ollama model info), but `selectLanguageModels` still resolves providers. The new endpoint objects are transient and not cached; no new positive/negative cache or boundary miss behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds one transient endpoint construction and several metadata objects/promises per discovered model; low confidence that this lightweight in-process work crosses the reporting threshold.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: OpenRouter can return a broad catalogue, but repository evidence does not establish that transient endpoint construction is costly enough relative to the pre-existing network discovery and catalogue parsing to create a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added O(model-count) allocation is avoidable eager work, but it performs no new boundary operation and available evidence does not establish concrete latency, CPU, or GC impact beyond a speculative optimization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending a genuine follow-up chat turn to an opted-in Chat Completions model such as Kimi K3
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Prompt rendering walks historical tool-call rounds, now retains same-model thinking for opted-in Chat Completions endpoints, serializes it into the existing request body, and sends the single model request; all are on response latency's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the chat-completions request containing conversation history and replayable historical thinking
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network request per user turn; no extra calls are introduced. Payload size grows with the effective number and byte size of same-model historical thinking rounds that survive prompt rendering/summarization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one request was sent, but historical Chat Completions thinking was omitted while assistant/tool history remained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request payload must be rendered, serialized, uploaded, and processed before the follow-up response streams.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Same-model historical tool/final rounds and their thinking text/opaque metadata, bounded by the prompt renderer's context budget and any summarization/compaction policy.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Historical rounds are rendered within one prompt and serialized into one request; there is no per-round network fan-out or new request concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Replay can preserve the model-visible history/prefix for supported models; the same-model and API-type guards prevent cross-model or unknown-protocol replay. Cold and warm requests have the same request count; any provider prompt-cache benefit depends on the remote service.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that payload bytes and serialization work increase in proportion to retained reasoning; high confidence this is the direct, required behavior of preserving reasoning rather than an accidental extra pass or duplicate boundary call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reasoning can materially enlarge long-history payloads, especially for custom endpoints whose existing serializer emits compatibility aliases, but exact history sizes, provider compression, token accounting, and cache effects are not established here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The larger payload is the feature's required semantic data, is gated to compatible/same-model history, and the diff neither adds network calls nor establishes an avoidable unbounded copy independent of that requirement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Registering provider protocol/adaptive-thinking metadata and selecting extension-contributed models across the proposed VS Code API
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider metadata is converted in the extension host, transferred over the existing provider RPC, cached in the workbench, then converted back into the selected `LanguageModelChat` API object before Copilot constructs its endpoint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer language-model metadata through the existing extension-host/main-thread language-model provider bridge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing RPC response per provider resolution with two additional scalar fields per model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The metadata record crossed the same RPC without `apiType` and `adaptiveThinking`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selection waits for metadata transport, but no additional round trip is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of model metadata records returned by a provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Conversion is synchronous per model inside the existing catalogue map; provider resolutions retain existing per-vendor sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selected models remain in `_localModels`/workbench model caches under existing invalidation rules; the new scalar fields do not create a separate cache or alter cache lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and unchanged RPC cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only a few bytes and constant-time enum/object mapping are added per model; no evidence indicates measurable transport or allocation impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is bounded metadata enrichment on an existing transport, not a new expensive boundary or materially amplified serialization path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and traced model discovery, capability transport, endpoint construction, prompt rendering, serialization, and chat request boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
